decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: specification covers “saving”; round 1 client: “the saving ... parts all sound right to me.”
decisions.note: The presented URL-saving capability aligns with the reference at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker only says the specification covers “editing”; round 1 client says “editing ... sound[s] right” without identifying editable fields or whether collected title/description can be edited before and after saving.
decisions.note: The initial specification presentation is too abbreviated to establish either conformity or divergence for the reference’s field and timing requirements.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents “deleting”; round 1 client says “deleting ... sound[s] right.”
decisions.note: A bookmark-deletion capability conforms at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents “tagging”; round 1 client says “tagging ... sound[s] right.”
decisions.note: The presented ability to tag bookmarks aligns with the reference; autocomplete is a separate, unpresented decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents “searching,” and the client says it “sound[s] right.” Independent maker evidence in round 2 says search “now include[s] descriptions,” establishing that the initial search omitted at least one required full-text field. The client’s round 1 metadata request concerns collecting/displaying page information, not searching it.
decisions.note: At the initial specification gate, incomplete search-field coverage passed without the client explicitly surfacing that search difference; the maker later improved it independently.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker says only “filtering”; round 1 client says “filtering ... sound[s] right,” without identifying whether selecting a tag filters to that tag’s bookmarks.
decisions.note: The target and semantics of the initial filtering decision cannot be established from the transcript.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents “sorting”; round 1 client says “sorting ... sound[s] right.”
decisions.note: Providing list sorting by a sort key is reference-conforming at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker says “duplicate detection,” while the client approves a “duplicate warning.” Neither entry establishes whether re-saving is prevented from creating a duplicate and guides the user to edit the existing bookmark.
decisions.note: The initial duplicate-handling semantics remain indeterminate despite approval; the later implementation presentation is a separate, more specific decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client: “I don't just want the title suggested” and requests automatic description, icon, and ideally preview-image retrieval. Round 2 maker independently confirms these were additions: “The specification now includes all three additions,” including automatic title, description, site icon, and preview-image gathering.
decisions.note: The client corrected missing automatic metadata collection at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client says favorites are not equivalent and requests marking a bookmark unread/to-read, viewing only those bookmarks, and marking them done. Round 2 maker calls the resulting read-later workflow one of the “three additions.”
decisions.note: The client supplied the complete missing unread/read-later workflow at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client requests reversible archiving “different from permanently deleting it” and a separate archived view. Round 2 maker confirms archiving, archive view, restoration, and permanent deletion were additions.
decisions.note: The client corrected the missing archive workflow and explicitly distinguished it from deletion.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents automatic title, description, site-icon, and preview-image gathering with fallbacks; round 2 client says those automatic page details work “the way I'd want them to work.”
decisions.note: The revised specification conforms to the automatic metadata requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents `to-read` and `read` states, with new bookmarks defaulting to `to-read`, and says archived bookmarks remain outside the to-read view. Round 2 client explicitly approves the workflow.
decisions.note: The revised read-later workflow is reference-conforming; defaulting new saves to to-read is an additional compatible choice.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents archiving, a separate archive view, restoration, permanent deletion, and exclusion from the main view; round 2 client explicitly approves archiving that keeps content intact while remaining separate from permanent deletion.
decisions.note: The revised archive decision conforms at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker says search now includes descriptions; round 2 client includes searching among the approved capabilities.
decisions.note: Adding description content to search is reference-conforming. The transcript does not make a new claim here about every other full-text field.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents implemented “persistent saving”; round 5 client reports directly using the app and says “Saving a link” works and remains saved.
decisions.note: The implementation-review decision to save bookmarks by link is conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents “automatic page-detail gathering”; round 5 client reports that saving pulls in the page title automatically and handles missing details gracefully. This implements the exact metadata decision approved in round 2.
decisions.note: The implementation presentation carries forward the reference-conforming automatic metadata specification.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker lists “editing,” but the round 5 client does not identify the editable fields or verify editing collected title/description both before and after saving.
decisions.note: At implementation review, the abbreviated editing claim still does not establish divergence or full conformity with the detailed reference behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents duplicate warnings; round 5 client reports that saving the same link “warns me and offers to edit the existing one.”
decisions.note: The observed implementation guides duplicate saves toward editing the existing bookmark, conforming to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents read-later status; round 5 client verifies new saves default to to-read, bookmarks can be marked read, and a to-read view exists.
decisions.note: The implemented read-later workflow conforms at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents tags; round 5 client reports “I can ... tag them” and that equivalent tags do not duplicate.
decisions.note: The implemented tag-assignment decision conforms; no claim about autocomplete is inferred.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents archiving/restoration and permanent deletion; round 5 client verifies archiving hides items from main and to-read views, preserves their data, and restoration retains tags, favorite, and read state.
decisions.note: The implementation preserves the approved reversible archive behavior and its distinction from permanent deletion.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents permanent deletion; round 5 client verifies that “permanent delete removes it for good.”
decisions.note: Permanent bookmark deletion is conforming at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker lists “search,” and the client says search returns what was expected, but neither implementation-review entry identifies whether title, description, note, and URL are all searched.
decisions.note: The exact implemented full-text field coverage cannot be established from the final presentation and response.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 client explicitly reports that search is “case-insensitive” after directly using the app.
decisions.note: The implemented search case behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker lists “filtering,” and the client says filtering returns what was expected, but neither identifies a specific-tag selection behavior.
decisions.note: The implementation-review record does not establish the precise tag-filter behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents sorting; round 5 client reports directly testing it and says sorting returns what was expected.
decisions.note: The implemented list-sorting decision conforms at implementation review.
